implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control Policy (2024, revised and approved 2026-09-17, effective 2026-10-01) covers business IT and OT. OT access procedures (OT-PR-02) describe account requests, Gas Control approval for HMI roles, and quarterly reviews (moving from annual).

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider vendor (SOC 2 Type 2) for DMZ gateway accounts
implementation_statement: OT domain and SCADA application accounts are requested through the access ticket and approved by the Director of Gas Control for HMI roles. Gaps: OT and field device access is reviewed annually (last February 2026), not quarterly; the station HMIs at Compressor Stations 2, 4, and 5 use one shared operator login per station; OT accounts of departing staff are removed in 5 business days on average (P07: 6 of 25 sampled terminations exceeded 1 business day).
evidence: OT domain export; SCADA user list; access review February 2026; termination sample (P07)

implementation_statement: Business IT and DMZ gateway accounts are created and disabled automatically from the HR system feed. OT domain and SCADA accounts are managed manually from the same ticket; automation is planned for 2027 with an OT identity bridge that does not create a domain trust.
evidence: IdP provisioning logs; OT account tickets

implementation_statement: Inactive OT accounts are disabled after 90 days by a quarterly script. Remote access gateway accounts expire after 60 days of inactivity. Gap: SCADA application accounts are not covered by the script (4 inactive accounts found in P07).
evidence: Disable script log; P07 AC-2 test

implementation_statement: SCADA application roles (viewer, controller, supervisor, engineer, administrator) enforce what each user can see and command. Controllers can command only the pipeline areas assigned to their console. Lateral owners have view-only accounts for their own laterals.
evidence: SCADA role matrix; role assignment export

implementation_statement: Firewall pairs at the GCC and BCC enforce one-way historian replication from OT to the DMZ and outbound-only TLS from the DMZ replica to the cloud OT analytics account. No business IT system can open a session into OT. Rule review is quarterly.
evidence: Firewall rule export 2026-07; quarterly rule review

implementation_statement: Duties are separated between controllers (operate), SCADA engineers (configure), and OT Security Engineers (security tools and access). Gap: two SCADA engineers can both change SCADA configuration and approve their own changes in the change tool; compensating control is the Director of Gas Control sign-off in the management of change process.
evidence: SCADA role matrix; change tool settings; MOC records

implementation_statement: Least privilege applies to SCADA roles and OT domain groups. Gaps: 9 OT domain administrator accounts against a target of 4; the compressor OEM service account on unit control panels has full rights.
evidence: OT privileged account list; P07 AC-6 test

implementation_statement: SCADA engineers and OT administrators use separate privileged accounts only from the engineering workstations and the remote access gateway; daily work uses non-privileged accounts.
OT privileged accounts are limited to named SCADA and OT staff. Gap: privileged account count above target and the OEM service account (AC-6).

The identity provider and remote access gateway lock accounts after 5 failed attempts. Tailored: HMI consoles do not lock out controllers, because a lockout during an abnormal operating condition is a safety risk; compensated by badge-controlled, staffed control rooms and CCTV (PE-3, PE-6).
evidence: Gateway policy; HMI tailoring decision in this SSP

implementation_statement: A system use banner is shown at OT domain logon and on the remote access gateway.

Engineering workstations and DMZ servers lock after 15 minutes. Tailored: HMI consoles in staffed control rooms do not lock, so controllers never lose the alarm display; station HMIs lock after 15 minutes.
Remote access gateway sessions end after 8 hours or 30 minutes of inactivity. HMI sessions are tailored out (AC-11).

provider_if_inherited: Remote access gateway vendor; identity provider vendor
implementation_statement: All staff and vendor remote access to OT goes through the DMZ remote access gateway with individual accounts, MFA, approval by the shift supervisor for each vendor session, and session recording. Gap: the compressor OEM remote diagnostics connections to unit control panels bypass the gateway and are not in the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan (P07 found an undocumented cellular modem at Compressor Station 4).
evidence: Gateway configuration; session approval log; P07 AC-17 test

implementation_statement: Gateway sessions are logged to the SIEM and recorded; the MSSP alerts on sessions outside approved windows. The OEM paths are not monitored.

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Gateway sessions use TLS 1.2 or higher end to end.
The remote access gateways at the GCC and BCC are the only approved access points into OT. Gap: OEM diagnostics paths (AC-17).
No wireless networks inside OT. Wireless at stations is business IT only, on a separate firewall zone. Quarterly wireless scans at control centers.
Field tablets are company-managed with encryption and remote wipe and have no OT access.

Personal devices may not connect to OT. Vendor laptops connect only to the gateway, never directly. Gap: OEM technicians plug laptops into unit control panels during site visits without a scan at 2 stations.
Security awareness and training policy and procedures are part of POL-01 and POL-05.
Annual awareness training and quarterly phishing simulations for all staff (June 2026 click rate 6.1%). Includes SSI handling and reporting of suspected incidents.

Controllers train on 3 cyber-caused abnormal operating conditions (loss of SCADA, false data, forced manual operation). SCADA engineers and OT Security Engineers complete OT security courses. Gap: compressor station technicians have no OT security training, though they operate station HMIs.
Training records are kept in the LMS and in the 192.631 compliance records.
POL-03 and the logging and monitoring standard (STD-02) set event, review, and retention requirements.

Logged events: OT domain logons and changes, SCADA application security and command events, firewall and gateway events, OT sensor alerts. Gaps: station HMIs at 3 stations and field devices do not send logs.
SCADA and OT domain records include user, time, source, event, and outcome.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews alerts 24x7; the Security Manager reviews a weekly OT report. Gap: there is no review of SCADA command logs against controller shift logs.
evidence: Weekly OT report; MSSP monthly report

implementation_statement: All OT servers and HMIs synchronize to GPS-disciplined time sources at the GCC and BCC.
Logs are forwarded to the SIEM, where only the MSSP and the Security Manager can delete them.
Business IT logs are kept 12 months. Gap: OT logs are kept 90 days, against the company 12-month standard; the archive tier for OT logs is planned for 2026-12-31.
Logging is enabled on SCADA servers, HMIs at the GCC and BCC, firewalls, and the gateway. Gap: station HMIs at 3 stations and field devices.

The TSA-approved Cybersecurity Assessment Plan schedules assessment of all Cybersecurity Implementation Plan measures over 3 years. The co-sourced internal audit firm performs the assessments; P07 is this year main assessment. Gap: 28% of measures assessed in the plan year to date against the one-third minimum.
Assessments are performed by the co-sourced internal audit firm, which does not design or operate any assessed control.

Interconnections are documented for the cloud OT analytics account, the customer activities website, interconnecting pipelines (phone and data), and the two OSA laterals. Gap: no written interconnection terms with the compressor OEM.
The POA&M tracks all P07, P03, and TSA inspection findings with milestones; reported quarterly to the audit committee.
The COO authorizes operation of the PSGCS as system owner; the CEO accepts High risks (section 4.2 of this SSP).
Monthly security metrics and quarterly POA&M review. Gap: continuous monitoring does not cover 3 compressor stations and field sites.
Annual external and internal penetration testing of business IT and the DMZ (last 2026-03). A purple team exercise on the remote access path is planned for 2027 Q1. No active testing on live OT.
Internal connections between OT zones (control centers, stations, field) are documented in the zone model of the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan. Gap: OEM paths missing.
Configuration management procedures for OT are in the SCADA change procedure and the MOC process.
Baseline configurations exist for SCADA servers, HMIs, and DMZ servers. Gap: no baseline for station PLC logic at 3 stations.

SCADA and network changes go through the MOC process with Director of Gas Control sign-off. Gaps: point-to-point verification records missing for 3 of 25 sampled SCADA changes; model vendor updates to the leak-detection model bypass MOC.
evidence: MOC records; SCADA change history; P07

control_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes
implementation_statement: SCADA changes are tested on the development SCADA server before release. Station PLC changes are not tested offline.
Security impact is part of the MOC form. Gap: the two 2025 permanent changes (OT analytics account, gateway vendor) were not assessed for TSA plan amendment.
Only the SCADA engineering role can change SCADA configuration, and only from the engineering workstations.
Hardening settings from the SCADA vendor guide applied to servers and control center HMIs. Gap: station HMIs not hardened at 3 stations.
Unused ports and services disabled on SCADA servers. Gap: station HMIs run unneeded services.
Application allowlisting enforced on GCC and BCC HMIs and engineering workstations. Not on station HMIs.
OT asset inventory covers servers, HMIs, network devices, and about 85% of field devices; firmware unknown for about 20% of RTUs and PLCs. P07 found an undocumented OEM cellular modem.
evidence: OT inventory export; P07 CM-8 test

implementation_statement: OT sensors detect new devices at the GCC, BCC, and Compressor Stations 1 and 3. Not at other sites.
Users cannot install software on HMIs or OT servers; allowlisting blocks it at control centers.
Contingency planning is covered by the emergency plan (192.615), the manual operation plan, and the Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan.

The emergency plan, manual operation plan, and BCC failover procedure cover loss of SCADA. Gap: criteria for a precautionary shutdown are not tied to the BIA (fixed in P08 runbook 1, adoption pending).
evidence: Emergency plan; manual operation plan; P05

implementation_statement: The Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan and the emergency plan reference each other; the Director of Gas Control signs both.
Controllers and shift supervisors train each year on BCC failover and manual operation.
BCC failover tested 2025-11-04; manual operation communication plan tested 2025-10. Gap: no full SCADA server rebuild from backup in the last 12 months.
Monthly offline SCADA backups are stored at the BCC, about 90 miles from the GCC.
The BCC at Compressor Station 3 is a hot standby with 6 HMIs; it can run the whole pipeline and both laterals.
Private microwave between control centers and stations; MPLS and cellular for field sites; satellite backup at 12 critical sites. Gap: 41 cellular sites rely on one carrier.
SCADA servers are backed up weekly online and monthly offline; configuration files after each change. Gap: PLC logic backups missing for Compressor Stations 2, 4, and 5.
evidence: Backup job logs; PLC backup register

implementation_statement: Backups are hash-checked and malware-scanned when made. Restore of configuration files tested quarterly; full rebuild not tested in 12 months.
Rebuild procedures exist for SCADA servers and HMIs. Not tested end to end in the last 12 months.
Identification and authentication procedures are in POL-02 and the authenticator standard (STD-06).
Individual accounts for SCADA, OT domain, and gateway users. Gap: shared station HMI logins at Compressor Stations 2, 4, and 5 (12 HMIs).

MFA is required for all privileged remote access through the gateway. At GCC and BCC engineering workstations, privileged logons use smart cards. Gap: privileged logons at station HMIs use passwords only.

Non-privileged remote access uses MFA. Controllers at HMIs in staffed, badge-controlled control rooms use passwords; this is the compensating control documented in the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan as SD 02G III.C.2 allows for 49 CFR 192 control rooms. Station HMIs have no documented compensating control.
evidence: Cybersecurity Implementation Plan section C.2; badge reports

implementation_statement: The identity provider uses replay-resistant authentication (push with number matching or security keys).
Field devices are identified by address and protocol at the SCADA host. Gap: no device authentication on legacy serial protocols.

The Cybersecurity Implementation Plan sets password resets every 12 months for OT accounts and every 24 months for field devices, with mitigations where reset is not possible. Gap: about 40% of field devices are past the schedule and the mitigation timeframe expired 2026-06-30.
OT passwords follow the 14-character rule and banned list on the OT domain. Field devices cannot enforce length; mitigations listed per device type.
Vendor and lateral owner users have individual accounts on the gateway or the SCADA viewer role.
POL-03 and the TSA Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan.
Incident response training each year for the incident response team, controllers, and shift supervisors.
Annual exercise tests at least two plan objectives with the positions named in the plan (2025: containment and IT/OT isolation, tabletop). Gap: isolation has never been performed live.
Incident handling follows the plan and the P08 runbooks. Gap: OT forensic capability at stations without sensors is limited; shutdown criteria not tied to BIA.
The MSSP uses an orchestration platform with playbooks for business IT containment. OT playbooks notify only; no automated OT actions by design.
All incidents are tracked in the incident register with severity and timeline.
The Cybersecurity Coordinator reports cybersecurity incidents to CISA within 72 hours; 2 reports made in 2025-2026 (phishing account compromise; malware on a field tablet), both within 24 hours.

provider_if_inherited: MSSP; incident response retainer firm with OT experience
implementation_statement: 24x7 MSSP support and an incident response retainer with OT capability through the insurer panel.
The Cybersecurity Incident Response Plan names positions and resources for each measure. Gap: precautionary shutdown criteria (P08) not yet adopted into the plan.
Maintenance of SCADA and station equipment is scheduled and recorded in the work management system.
Remote maintenance by the SCADA vendor and integrator uses the gateway with approval and recording. Gap: OEM remote diagnostics outside the gateway.
Vendor technicians are escorted at control centers and stations and listed in the visitor log.
Removable media in OT is limited to scanned, company-issued media.
SSI is marked with the 49 CFR 1520.13 protective marking and distribution limitation statement. Gap: copies of TSA plans and the 2025 assessment report found unmarked on a general file share.
SSI and Restricted OT records are stored in the restricted SSI repository and locked cabinets.
Retired OT drives and devices are wiped or destroyed with certificates.
USB scanning kiosks at the GCC, BCC, and all 5 stations; unscanned media is blocked on control center HMIs.
Control room access lists are approved by the Director of Gas Control and reviewed quarterly.
Badge access with CCTV at the GCC, BCC, and station control rooms; field sites locked and alarmed. This is the compensating control for control room HMI authentication.
Physical access alarms at control rooms and M&R stations go to the GCC shift supervisor.
Visitor logs at control centers and stations kept 2 years.
UPS and generators at the GCC, BCC, and stations, tested monthly.
Fire detection and suppression in both control center server rooms.
This SSP; the TSA Cybersecurity Implementation Plan is the regulator-facing plan and references this SSP for control detail.
POL-05 rules of behavior acknowledged each year.
Zone-based architecture (control centers, stations, field, DMZ, business) reviewed by a third-party architecture design review in 2025.

baseline: Not in High baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring (not in the High baseline). POL-01 and the program plan cover IT and OT.

baseline: Not in High baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. The Security Manager leads the program and is the primary Cybersecurity Coordinator; alternates are an OT Security Engineer and the IT Director.

baseline: Not in High baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. Risk appetite and acceptance authorities approved by the CEO and audit committee (P01).

baseline: Not in High baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Selected by tailoring. The BIA (P05) defines business critical functions as the TSA definition requires.
Background checks for all staff with OT or SSI access; vendors attest for their technicians.
Business IT access ends automatically at termination. Gap: OT account removal averages 5 business days; shared station passwords are not changed when a station technician leaves.
Transfers trigger an access review. Gap: 3 of 15 sampled transfers kept SCADA roles they no longer needed.
Contracts with the SCADA vendor, integrator, and MSSP require named technicians and notice of departures. Gap: the OEM contract has no such terms.
Position descriptions define controller, SCADA engineer, and OT security duties and authority, consistent with 192.631(b).
FIPS 199 categorization in section 6 of this SSP.
Annual risk assessment per SP 800-30 covering IT and OT (P01, 2026-07).
Supplier risk is assessed at onboarding. Gap: 10 of 14 Tier 1 vendors have no current assessment.

Monthly authenticated scans of business IT and the DMZ; OT vulnerabilities tracked passively from sensors and vendor advisories (no active scanning in OT). Gap: 6 CISA KEV entries on OT components past the mitigation timeline.
Critical Cyber Systems CCS-1 to CCS-8 identified in the Cybersecurity Implementation Plan from the BIA.
The security addendum is required for new OT purchases since 2025. Gap: legacy OEM and telecom contracts lack it.

provider_if_inherited: MSSP; SCADA software vendor; telecom carrier
implementation_statement: External services are listed in the vendor register with tier. SOC 2 reviewed for 4 of 14 Tier 1 vendors.
14 station HMIs run an operating system past end of support; compensating controls (no internet path, allowlisting planned, isolated VLAN) are documented for 6; replacement funded for 2027.

provider_if_inherited: Telecom carrier; customer activities website vendor
implementation_statement: Carrier DDoS protection for internet circuits; the customer activities website vendor provides DDoS protection.
Firewall pairs separate business IT, the DMZ, and OT at both control centers; stations connect to control centers only over the private microwave and MPLS.
Access points into OT are limited to the two DMZs. Gap: OEM cellular path at Compressor Station 4.
Carrier MPLS and cellular private network services are under contract with traffic separation. Gap: no security terms or incident notice in the cellular contract.

control_name: Deny by Default — Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: All OT firewall rule sets deny by default; each allow rule has an owner and a review date.

OT traffic does not traverse business IT. Traffic between control centers and stations crosses the private microwave unencrypted; MPLS links are encrypted. Field polling over cellular uses the carrier private network without end-to-end encryption.
IPsec on MPLS and DMZ-to-cloud links. Encryption of the microwave backbone is planned for 2027.
Keys for cloud OT analytics data are customer-managed in the cloud key service.
Approved algorithms per the encryption standard (STD-08).
SCADA backups and engineering laptops are encrypted at rest.
Patch strategy with risk ranking and CISA KEV priority: OT patches applied quarterly after vendor qualification. Gap: 6 KEV entries past mitigation timeline; station HMIs unsupported.
Anti-malware with offline signature updates on GCC and BCC servers and HMIs. Gap: station HMIs at 3 stations have outdated signatures.
Passive OT sensors at 4 sites with MSSP alerting on new devices, new connections, and command anomalies. Gap: 3 stations and field sites unmonitored; no field telecom baseline.

control_name: Automated Tools and Mechanisms for Real-time Analysis
implementation_statement: The MSSP correlates SIEM and sensor alerts in real time.
CISA advisories, TSA information circulars, and vendor advisories are reviewed weekly.
SCADA server binaries are hash-checked monthly. PLC logic integrity is checked only where backups exist (2 of 5 stations).
Email filtering blocks spam and phishing before delivery; no email access from OT.
192.631 records and TSA plan records kept per the records schedule.
A supply chain risk section is in POL-01 and the vendor standard (STD-03, draft).
OT purchases go through the security addendum and acceptance testing. Gap: OEM-installed components bypass acceptance.
Approved supplier list for SCADA and network equipment. Not applied to OEM-supplied communications gear.
Tier 1 suppliers reviewed annually from SOC 2 or questionnaire; 4 of 14 done.
MSSP and SCADA vendor contracts require incident notice within 24 hours. Gap: OEM and cellular carrier contracts have no notice term.
Field devices and network gear bought only from authorized distributors. Not verified for OEM-supplied modems.
